implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX, aliased into ESI at 0x00a85791 and never moved back; ONE ordinary stack word, declared and left unnamed, that no instruction in the 64 reads. That word exists because the terminator is `RET 0x4` (bytes C2 04 00) and abi_derived inference A1-IMM states at APPROXIMATION confidence that the slot is 'derived from the terminal immediate alone; no argument read was observed, so this is the popped area and not a parameter count'; ordinary_stack_arguments[0] carries {read false, written false, observed false, source ret_immediate}. The model test drives four different values through it and asserts the receiver's bytes and the transfer sequence are identical for all four.
implementation.return_type: void -- chosen deliberately, and the disagreement with the canonical record is recorded in return_semantics and known_blockers rather than papered over. The single return site 0x00a85838 is reached from four directions and the word in EAX is a DIFFERENT unrelated value on each: the caller's own EAX on both early-exit paths (0x00a85797, 0x00a857a5, neither of which is preceded by an EAX write), the negative word just tested at 0x00a85824, and whatever the 0x00a8582f callee returned on the fallthrough. No path puts a value this function computed into EAX and no single value is consistent across paths, so the body produces no return value. Ghidra's own decompilation agrees in substance: signature `undefined FUN_00a85790(void)`, body ends in a bare `return;`, return_type_resolved false.
implementation.receiver_model: an OPAQUE byte run of 0x6c bytes and nothing else. NO STRUCT MEMBER IS NAMED anywhere in the package, because the machine-derived receiver record for this target is `bounds_only: true` (abi_derived.value.receiver: {bounds_only true, confidence INFERRED, distinct_offsets 4, max_offset 104, offsets [12,16,20,104], present true, register ECX, shape R-ALIAS, written_through 2}), and a bounds_only record states how far the body was seen reaching and not which member is which. Every access goes through a displacement-named accessor (byte_at / half_at / word_at / store_byte / store_word / load_slot / load_listener_slot) whose displacement is a named constexpr annotated with the instruction it came from. The 0x6c size is this body's own bound, not a second listing's: 0x00a85831 is `MOV dword ptr [ESI + 0x68], 0xffffffff`, an eleven-byte dword store whose last byte is at +0x6b. The record's own max_offset is 104 (0x68), which is the START of that store and would understate the requirement on its own. The words at receiver+0x10 and receiver+0x0c are NOT declared pointer members either: the body uses each as an ADDRESS, and the header hands both back as `Word` values so a two-level dereference is writable two levels deep and a one-level one is not writable at all.
implementation.dispatch_model: four indirect transfers, all `CALL reg`, all reaching their target through a THREE-step chase that the model performs as three separate reads. Step 1 is the word at receiver+0x10 (a pointer value, L); step 2 is the word L leads with (the table base, T); step 3 is a displacement in T. The four sites: 0x00a857e6 -> slot displacement 0x18, no stack argument, ECX = L; 0x00a85815 and 0x00a8581d -> slot displacement 0x1c, two pushed words, ECX = L, callee pops 8; 0x00a8582f -> slot displacement 0x14, one pushed word, ECX = L, callee pops 4. The record agrees on the count: abi_derived.value.dispatch is {indirect_calls 4, call_offsets [], vtable_shaped_loads 0}. The three callee shapes are separated by the STACK, not by taste: nothing is pushed before 0x00a857e6 and nothing is popped after it, so that callee takes no stack word; two words are pushed on both 0x1c arms and 0x00a8581d is followed by a fallthrough to 0x00a8581f with no pop at all while 0x00a85815's `POP EDI` at 0x00a85817 is the frame's own restore, so that callee must pop its own eight; and 0x00a8582f pushes one word with no pop after it. Whether the three displacements are VTABLE SLOTS or plain callback words inside an object is NOT claimed: both readings execute the same instructions. The slot INDICES (5, 6, 7) are recorded in the header as the arithmetic 0x14/4, 0x18/4, 0x1c/4 and are asserted by nothing.
implementation.dependency_note: the one direct callee 0x00a85460 is declared extern in the package header and defined as an observer in this package's own model test. Its callsite fixes its shape and nothing else: 0x00a857c9 `MOV ECX,ESI` puts the RECEIVER in the receiver register one instruction before 0x00a857cb and the only PUSH before that call is the prologue's, so no stack argument is passed. Its return type is declared void because THIS BODY discards whatever it leaves in EAX -- 0x00a857d0 reloads EAX from the receiver before anything can observe it -- which is a statement about the callsite's evidence and not about 0x00a85460, whose own body this package has not reconstructed. mechanics.body_shape: one entry, one exit, one return site, four early exits into it. 9 conditional branches (8 JZ + 1 JNZ + 1 JL -- see control_flow for the exact list) and 1 unconditional JMP, every target inside the span, so the branch graph closes here. The body is a nested if, not a state machine: the notification block is entered on (bit 3 OR bit 5) of a flag word and skipped to a shared continuation otherwise, and the pending-identifier half is that continuation.

frame_resolution.method: ESP is walked once from entry. The only stack effect before the terminator is the prologue's PUSH ESI at 0x00a85790 and its matching POP ESI at 0x00a85838, plus the two pushed words on each 0x1c arm (which the callee pops, since 0x00a85818 JMPs to 0x00a8581f with a balanced stack and 0x00a8581d is followed by a fallthrough with no pop at all) and the one pushed word before 0x00a8582f (callee-popped, since 0x00a85831 follows directly).

receiver_displacement.0x0c: READ at 0x00a857ab and 0x00a857d0 and 0x00a857e8 and 0x00a8581f's predecessor chain. Used as an ADDRESS in all four: the body never inspects it, it dereferences it at +0x08 (the flag word) and at +0xa8 (the halfword argument). So the flag word is TWO levels below the receiver and the halfword is two levels below it as well, through the same intermediate object.
receiver_displacement.0x10: READ at 0x00a8579d (the only null test in the body), 0x00a857de, 0x00a85805 and 0x00a85826. Used as an ADDRESS in the last four: the object L it points at leads with a table base at +0x00, and the three dispatches read that table at +0x14, +0x18 and +0x1c. Never written.
receiver_displacement.0x14: READ at 0x00a85793 and WRITTEN at 0x00a857a1 (one byte, value 0). This is the one-shot arm. The store happens on every path that gets past 0x00a85797, including the path that then returns because L is null.
receiver_displacement.0x28: ADDRESSED at 0x00a85810 by `LEA EDI,[ESI + 0x28]` and pushed as the second argument of the 0x1c call on the bit-6-set arm. Never read and never written by this body; the model passes the address, never the contents.
receiver_displacement.0x68: READ at 0x00a8581f and WRITTEN at 0x00a85831 (one dword, value 0xffffffff). The signed test at 0x00a85824 is on this word, and the sentinel the body stores is exactly the word that test rejects, which is what makes the second half of the function idempotent.

layout_derivation.note: NO FIELD LAYOUT IS DERIVED. The machine receiver record is bounds_only, so the package names no member and asserts no sub-object type. What follows is the bound, and it is this body's own.
layout_derivation.record 0x6c bytes: 0x00a85831 is `MOV dword ptr [ESI + 0x68], 0xffffffff`, opcode C7 46 68 FF FF FF FF -- seven bytes (C7, modrm 46 = [ESI + disp8], disp8 0x68, four immediate bytes), so a DWORD store ending at +0x6b. The body needs 0x6c bytes to exist. The listing corroborates the count: 0x00a85831 + 7 = 0x00a85838, the next instruction. The record's own max_offset is 104 (0x68), the START of that store, so the record alone understates it by four.
layout_derivation.largest read on the receiver: 0x68. The 0xa8 reads are on the SOURCE object, which is a different object reached through receiver+0x0c, and 0x28 is an address computation rather than a read.
layout_derivation.out of bounds: nothing. Every displacement the body forms is 0x0c, 0x10, 0x14, 0x28 or 0x68 on the receiver, 0x08 and 0xa8 on the source, and 0x14, 0x18 and 0x1c in the listener's table.

mechanics.control_flow: nine conditional branches, all 6-byte Jcc, plus one 2-byte JMP. 0x00a85797 JZ -> 0x00a85838 (arm already clear: total no-op). 0x00a857a5 JZ -> 0x00a85838 (listener word null: arm cleared, nothing else). 0x00a857b9 JNZ -> 0x00a857c5 (bit 3 set: enter the notification block). 0x00a857c3 JZ -> 0x00a8581f (bit 3 and bit 5 both clear: skip the block). 0x00a857c7 JZ -> 0x00a857d0 (bit 0 clear: skip the direct call). 0x00a857dc JZ -> 0x00a857e8 (bit 3 clear on the reload: skip slot 0x18). 0x00a857f6 JZ -> 0x00a8581f (bit 5 clear on the reload: skip slot 0x1c). 0x00a8580d JZ -> 0x00a8581a (bit 6 clear: the second argument is a real null word). 0x00a85824 JL -> 0x00a85838 (the pending word is negative: stop). 0x00a85818 JMP -> 0x00a8581f (after the slot-0x1c call with a real second argument). The single return site 0x00a85838 is reached from 0x00a85797, 0x00a857a5, 0x00a85824 and the fallthrough; the single continuation 0x00a8581f is reached from 0x00a857c3, 0x00a857f6, 0x00a85818 and the fallthrough.
mechanics.arm_decision: the gate is an OR of two bits, tested in that order and short-circuiting: bit 3 jumps into the block at 0x00a857c5, and only if bit 3 is clear is bit 5 tested, and only if bit 5 is ALSO clear does the body jump past the whole block. Inside the block the two dispatches are gated on their own bits ALONE -- bit 3 again at 0x00a857d9, bit 5 again at 0x00a857f3 -- each on a FRESHLY RELOADED flag word, and the direct call is gated on bit 0 alone at 0x00a857c5. The 0xa8 halfword's bit decides only the second argument, never whether the call happens.
mechanics.exact_find_not_lower_bound: the flag word is re-read from memory THREE times (0x00a857ae, 0x00a857d3, 0x00a857eb) and each read follows a call, so a callee that writes the flag word changes what a later gate does. The model re-reads at each of the three points and the model test drives a mutating direct callee (case 06) and a mutating slot-0x18 observer (case 07) to prove the three reads are three reads.
mechanics.not_modelled: EAX, and the reason is a fact rather than an omission: the body writes EAX eleven times and reloads it from the receiver after each of the three calls (0x00a857d0, 0x00a857e8, 0x00a8581f), so no callee's return value reaches a branch, a store or a push. The model keeps no EAX word and the model test runs the same scenario with four different observer return values (0, 1, all-ones, 0x0badc0de) and requires an identical transfer sequence, which is the strongest statement the evidence allows. EDX is likewise modelled as a scratch register with no word of its own: every read of it follows its nearest write with no CALL in between. EDI IS modelled, with an explicit word, because 0x00a8580f/0x00a85817 is a real save and restore pair around a call and its effect is observable; see mechanics.edi_note.
mechanics.edi_note: 0x00a8580f PUSH EDI and 0x00a85817 POP EDI bracket ONLY the 0x00a85815 call. The word they preserve is whatever EDI held on entry to the push, because the body writes EDI nowhere else in its 64 instructions. The reason the pair exists is visible two instructions earlier: 0x00a85810 computes `LEA EDI,[ESI + 0x28]`, an interior pointer into the receiver, and 0x00a85813 pushes it -- an optimiser preserving a callee-saved register across a call that nothing after 0x00a85817 needs it for. The observable is exact: after the 0x1c call returns, EDI holds what it held before, whatever the callee did in between; and the 0x00a8581d arm has NO such pair, so nothing about EDI is preserved there. The model threads one explicit EDI word (edi_register / set_edi_register) so both halves are falsifiable, and the model test drives an observer that scribbles on it and checks both directions (case 14).
mechanics.globals: none, and it is an evidenced absence rather than a silence: the complete 64-instruction listing names no data-segment address. Every address the body forms is `[ESI + disp]`, `[[ESI + disp] + disp]`, a `LEA` of the first, or a table word reached through one of those. The only immediates in the body are 0 (three times: the two CMPs and the PUSH at 0x00a8581a), 0x1 (the two TEST masks), the shift amounts 3, 5 and 6, the displacements, and 0xffffffff at 0x00a85831. The xref export carries no data-reference edge type at all, so there is nothing to corroborate a global against -- and nothing to corroborate is needed for an absence.

direct_call_1.arguments: the receiver, in ECX. 0x00a857c9 is `MOV ECX,ESI` and nothing is pushed between it and the call (the only earlier PUSH is the prologue's at 0x00a85790). No stack argument.
direct_call_1.cleanup: not observable from this callsite: nothing is pushed and nothing is popped, so a zero-argument callee-clean signature and a zero-argument caller-clean signature are indistinguishable here.
direct_call_1.return: discarded. 0x00a857d0 reloads EAX from the receiver one instruction later, so no value this callee returns is observable in this body.
direct_call_1.gate: reachable only when (flag bit 3 OR flag bit 5) AND flag bit 0, all from the FIRST read of the flag word at 0x00a857ae. Bit 0 is the only gate: this call is inside the notification block, so a flag word carrying bit 0 alone never reaches it.
direct_call_1.callee_record: none. There is no evidence pack for 0x00a85460 in this repository, so this package asserts nothing about it beyond what its own callsite's five bytes fix. See unresolved_questions.

mechanics.return_semantics_machine: return_register EAX (inference RT1, INFERRED); return_semantics unclassified_in_EAX; RT2 reads the last EAX write as register_class aggregate_unknown, which is accurate: the last EAX write on the fallthrough path is 0x00a8582c `MOV EAX,dword ptr [EDX + 0x14]`, a load of a table word that is then called, so what EAX holds at the RET is that callee's return value, whose width and meaning this body cannot see. The Ghidra decompiler's own reading is `return;` with return_type undefined and return_type_resolved false. REPRODUCED against the validator's evidence module in this repair session, the same three states this sidecar's four-path argument names are the ones the machine-return engine computes: UNDEFINED on the 0x00a85797 and 0x00a857a5 paths, DEFINED-4 on the 0x00a85824 path, and NOT BOUNDABLE on the fallthrough path because the 0x00a8582f CALL EAX result is the callee's. That is why the machine state is UNCLASSIFIED and the dimension stops; see known_blockers.
mechanics.receiver_writes: exactly two, and the byte-diff in the model test asserts there are no others anywhere in a 0x280-byte guarded buffer. 0x00a857a1 writes ONE BYTE at +0x14, value 0, on every path past 0x00a85797. 0x00a85831 writes ONE DWORD at +0x68, value 0xffffffff, on the single path that reaches it. Nothing else in the 64 instructions writes memory.

return_semantics.kind: void (declared), against a canonical record of unclassified_in_EAX
return_semantics.declared_choice: option (b) of the two the worker contract allows: `void`, declared because the bytes genuinely produce nothing, NOT because the record's token was unmatchable. The four-path argument is in implementation.return_type and the header's return-type note. The package did NOT declare a typedef named after the machine phrase to win the validator's string comparison, and it did NOT invent a width; it declares what the listing shows and records the disagreement.
return_semantics.why_the_record_and_this_disagree: the record is not wrong, it is describing a register rather than a function. `unclassified_in_EAX` says 'a value comes back in EAX and this analysis cannot classify it'. On this body the value that comes back in EAX is never a value the function produced: it is the caller's own EAX on both early-exit paths, the negative word just tested on the third, and a callee's return on the fourth. Three different unrelated values at one return site is the signature of a function that returns nothing, which is also what the decompiler concluded when it emitted a bare `return;`.
return_semantics.known_consequence: the validator's RETURN SEMANTICS arm has no route to a verdict on this target from the source side. The machine-evidenced route computes its state from the listing and the ABI record alone and lands on UNCLASSIFIED (three EAX states over the four predecessors of the single return), and on that state it reports NOT_AVAILABLE whatever the span declares. The older string-comparison arm would own the target only if an ABI layer carried a canonical C `return_type`; `unclassified_in_EAX` is machine vocabulary, and no layer here carries a C type, so the comparison would be a WARN for any C++ declaration whatsoever, including a correct one. Declaring `void` is the honest maximum and the arm's NOT_AVAILABLE is the accurate name for 'the machine fixes no width here'. NOT_AVAILABLE is not a failure of this reconstruction. Recorded in known_blockers.

evidence.classification: DERIVED from the live evidence pack; LIVE at capture time
evidence.decompiler: Ghidra: `void __fastcall FUN_00a85790(int param_1) { ... return; }`, with the receiver modelled as a stack-passed `param_1` rather than as a hidden `this`. The record's ghidra_calling_convention is null and ghidra_calling_convention_signal is no_information, so the decompiler's own `__fastcall` spelling is cross-validation-only and is not followed: the listing's receiver-in-ECX plus `RET 0x4` is __thiscall, which is what the package declares.
evidence.decompiler_disagreements: three, and the listing is followed in all three. (1) The decompiler types the flag word's test as `uVar2 >> 3 & 1` and `uVar2 >> 5 & 1` on a local, i.e. it carries the flag word in a pseudo-variable; the listing re-loads it from memory at 0x00a857d0 and 0x00a857e8, and the model re-loads it, because the reloads are what let a callee change a later gate. (2) The decompiler evaluates the 0x1c call's second argument as `param_1 + 0x28` versus `0` in an if/else on `(uVar2 >> 6 & 1)`, which matches the listing, but it places the bit-6 test after the table loads; the listing computes it at 0x00a857ff/0x00a85802 and holds the flags live across 0x00a85805/0x00a85808/0x00a8580a to the JZ at 0x00a8580d, which is the same value and the model says so. (3) The decompiler writes the `[ESI + 0x68] = 0xffffffff` store as unconditional relative to its own `if (-1 < *(int *)(param_1 + 0x68))` guard, which is correct, but it renders the guard as `-1 < x` where the listing's `TEST EAX,EAX` + `JL` is a signed-zero-or-positive test on the whole word; these agree on every 32-bit input, and the model states the test as a sign-bit test because that is what the two instructions do.

refutation_families: D1 wrong constant / off-by-one displacement: decoys of the same shape at every neighbouring displacement in the receiver (0x08, 0x60, 0x64, 0x6c, and its own 0xa8), in the source (0x00, 0x04, 0xa4, 0xac) and in the listener's table (slots 0x10 and 0x20 either side of the three the body reads).
